answer: No. Your records show you did not have a blood clot in your lung. On 8 July 2025 you had chest pain and a blood test (D-dimer) that came back high at 0.92 (normal is 0.49 or less). A high D-dimer is not specific, so it led to a CT scan of the chest with contrast to look for a clot. That scan, which is the one you remember, found no pulmonary embolism and clear lungs. Your chart lists pulmonary embolism as 'ruled out'. The chest wall pain was recorded as resolved by 22 July 2025. The scan also showed mild wear-and-tear changes in the spine of your upper back, which is common.
short: A chest CT angiogram on 8 July 2025, done for chest pain and a raised D-dimer, showed no pulmonary embolism; the diagnosis is recorded as ruled out.
